batches.acceptance_evidence: Runtime and delivery evidence belong in the fixed ledger; matrix acceptance alone does not demonstrate execution.

evidence_requirements: Map each in-scope application's credential use to a vault-backed reference and its managed identity; provide redacted configuration, never secret values.
Identify any credentials remaining in source, environment configuration or deployment parameters and document the migration or explicit exception.
Reviewer decision: does the redacted application-to-vault map cover every relevant credential in this scope?
recommendations.limitations: Vault existence does not prove applications store or retrieve their credentials there. Application intent and redacted owner-provided integration evidence are required; no secret enumeration, repository credential scan or data-plane access is performed.

evidence_requirements: Provide the application/environment/region inventory and map each security or availability domain to its vault.
Identify intentionally shared vaults, their access boundaries and expected transaction demand; include the reviewed sharing justification.
Reviewer decision: does the vault partitioning respect each declared application, environment, regional and access boundary without an unreviewed shared blast radius?
recommendations.limitations: Resource names, vault counts and arbitrary request-rate thresholds do not establish application boundaries or adequate scaling. Architecture ownership and workload demand require human judgment; no workload traffic or secret contents are collected.

rule.coverage: Both explicit vault enableSoftDelete and enablePurgeProtection booleans are true. This proves configuration, not successful recovery or operational effectiveness.

evidence_requirements: Explicit enableSoftDelete and enablePurgeProtection booleans on the same canonical Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults instance using reviewed API 2024-11-01.
ARM and existing no-restore Bicep, saved normalized observed evidence and injected scoped management-plane GET are supported.
Raw Terraform and optional plan project the explicit purge flag but cannot establish soft-delete state for an imported or updated vault: the result remains unknown even when purge protection is true.
recommendations.limitations: Only explicit booleans on one vault are assessed; omitted/null/symbolic/wrong-type fields stay unknown. Both known true pass; either known false with the other known fails. Missing, inaccessible and stale evidence cannot pass. No vault targets are N/A only with complete relevant inventory; otherwise unknown. AzureRM 4.50.0 sets soft delete on creation, but raw configuration/plan values alone do not prove creation versus import/update, so no provider default or creation-only invariant is inferred.

evidence_requirements: Provide redacted vault RBAC scope/role assignments, privileged role eligibility and activation requirements, including approval and MFA settings.
Map operators and applications to their required actions; identify excessive standing privileges, legacy access policies and documented exceptions.
Reviewer decision: are privileged administrative rights least-privileged and eligible/JIT rather than unreviewed standing access? Use owner-supplied evidence; do not request new Graph/Entra access.
recommendations.limitations: An RBAC-enabled flag or role assignment alone does not demonstrate least privilege, PIM eligibility or activation controls. New Entra/PIM/Graph access is outside authorization; absent evidence is not a failing or passing least-privilege conclusion.

evidence_requirements: Map each vault to its chosen private-endpoint or permitted service-endpoint/firewall access pattern and the workloads allowed to reach it.

For private endpoints, supply redacted approval, vault/subnet identity, private DNS resolution and client-route evidence; for firewall alternatives, supply default action, allowed subnet/IP rules and reviewed trusted-service bypasses.
Reviewer decision: do the exact relationships and intended access path restrict the vault appropriately, including any public-access or trusted-service exception?
recommendations.limitations: A private endpoint, disabled-public flag or firewall rule in isolation does not prove approval, DNS, client reachability or the intended alternative access pattern. No network scans, client probes or remediation are performed.

evidence_requirements: Map each in-scope vault's enabled AuditEvent/allLogs diagnostic category to its exact destination Log Analytics workspace identity.
Identify which workspace the platform owner has designated as central and provide redacted retained-log/ingestion evidence from the owner.
Reviewer decision: do all relevant vaults send audit usage to the approved central workspace, rather than only metrics or an unrelated destination?
recommendations.limitations: Metrics are collected automatically but resource audit logs require routed diagnostic settings. Workspace existence or a diagnostic-setting name cannot prove audit-category selection, the approved central destination or ingestion. No Log Analytics/data-plane queries are executed.

rule.coverage: Explicit container soft-delete enablement on the exact default blob-service child. Not blob soft delete, account deletion protection, recovery success or an owner-specific retention duration.

evidence_requirements: Actual default blob-service child containerDeleteRetentionPolicy.enabled boolean using reviewed API 2023-05-01; a storage-account secure-transfer flag or blob deleteRetentionPolicy is not a substitute.

ARM and existing no-restore Bicep support explicit child resources; raw Terraform and optional plan support an explicit single blob_properties.container_delete_retention_policy block with an explicitly valid days value from 1 through 365 on AzureRM 4.50.0.
Saved normalized observed evidence and injected scoped management-plane GET of the default child are supported; no storage data-plane endpoint is contacted.
recommendations.limitations: A known explicit true passes and false fails. Missing child configuration, unresolved/omitted/invalid retention days, unsupported versions, denied or stale evidence stay unknown. Terraform block omission is not inferred as false and provider-default days are not inferred. Every known storage account missing a child receives an unresolved child, not an absence-based N/A. No blob targets are N/A only for complete relevant inventory with no storage accounts/children. FileStorage capability is not inferred from absence or failed reads. The current recommendation is enablement only: a seven-day preference or retention adequacy is not silently imposed.

evidence_requirements: Provide the relevant TLS policy definition/initiative, assignment scope, enforcement mode, effect, parameter values, exclusions and active exemptions for the exact storage-account population.
Compare explicit storage-account minimumTlsVersion values with that policy intent and original-time compliance results; identify inherited or inaccessible policy-definition gaps.
Reviewer decision: is the intended minimum TLS version actually enforced by the relevant effective policy configuration, not just configured on one account?
recommendations.limitations: The checklist requests Azure Policy enforcement. A minimumTlsVersion flag alone is only local configuration and cannot pass this recommendation. Assignments without relevant definitions, effects, parameters and population coverage are insufficient; old compliance timestamps are not refreshed. No policy changes, scans or evaluations are triggered.

batches.acceptance_evidence: Implementation, checks and merged delivery are separate ledger facts. Matrix classification is not delivery.

evidence_requirements: Provide explicit deployed/planned Azure Firewall sku.tier; a Firewall Policy SKU is not a substitute.
Use ARM/observed 2024-05-01 or explicit AzureRM 4.50.0 sku_tier. Missing, symbolic, null, wrong-type or unsupported tier/version stays unknown.
Premium passes this SKU configuration predicate; explicit Basic/Standard fails. Stale/denied/error and complete-empty versus partial-empty semantics remain unchanged.
recommendations.limitations: SKU capability only: no claim that Premium features are enabled, correctly configured or inspecting traffic. No region, licensing, runtime capacity or operational-effectiveness conclusion.
positive_negative_uncertainty_tests: Premium pass; Basic/Standard fail; invalid/missing tiers unknown
all promised adapters and existing no-restore Bicep
stale/partial/denied, exact identity comparison and replay

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Positive configured subnet/route-table references and matching inventory only; no effective-path verdict.
evidence_requirements: Identify workload subnets not connected to Virtual WAN and bind each to its actual route-table ID; exclude neither inaccessible nor unclassified subnets.
Provide 0.0.0.0/0 UDR, next-hop IP/type, canonical firewall/NVA mapping and representative effective-route evidence, including BGP/peering and more-specific route overrides.
Reviewer decision: does every applicable subnet's actual Internet path reach the intended inspection appliance? Explain Virtual WAN applicability and any intentional exceptions.
recommendations.limitations: An attached table, default route or VirtualAppliance label alone does not establish an effective inspected path. Positive references do not establish relationship completeness; no effective-route, packet or data-plane query is run.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Typed explicit diagnostic target/workspace and Dedicated/AzureDiagnostics destination facts when supplied.
evidence_requirements: Map each firewall to its diagnostic setting's exact target resource and workspace. Verify Dedicated destination with enabled relevant log categories/category groups; metric-only settings do not satisfy logging.
Provide attributable original-time evidence of records arriving in the resource-specific tables, including the reviewed category population, retention and any intentionally excluded traffic classes.
Reviewer decision: are all firewall deployments covered by functioning resource-specific log routing and storage, rather than only an unbound destination flag?
recommendations.limitations: The original structured-logs link now redirects to Monitor Azure Firewall. Explicit Terraform diagnostic subfacts are supported; arbitrary ARM extension-resource scope evaluation, complete diagnostic enumeration and log-ingestion/data-plane access are not added. Dedicated without a workspace cannot establish routing.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit firewall-to-policy reference, without a migration-complete judgment.
evidence_requirements: Identify firewalls using classic application, network and NAT collections; provide the pre-migration inventory and exact target policy association.
Reconcile every original rule/action/priority and inherited parent policy against the migrated rule collection groups; provide the change validation/rollback record without executing a migration.
Reviewer decision: where classic rules existed, is policy migration complete and functionally reconciled? If none existed, provide attributable applicability evidence.
recommendations.limitations: Association presence is not proof of rule equivalence, historic migration or active enforcement. Missing classic arrays and names cannot establish no migration was needed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Strict supplied IPv4 prefix capacity subcheck at /26 or larger, plus positive canonical firewall/subnet references.
evidence_requirements: Bind each VNet firewall's data and any management configuration to exact subnet IDs. Review the positive references alongside the prepared standalone subnet prefixes; unresolved/missing or duplicate joins remain visible.

Verify at least /26 IPv4 capacity (prefix length <=26) for every relevant data/management subnet; /24 is not a failure merely because the checklist says /26. Explain secured-hub versus customer-subnet applicability.
Reviewer decision: does the complete applicable firewall-subnet population meet capacity, including management subnets, rather than merely a subnet with a conventional name?
recommendations.limitations: The local capacity subcheck is not a whole-control pass. Positive links do not establish complete data/management association coverage. Inline VNet subnet expansion, IPAM allocation and IPv6 capacity are not claimed. Optional/missing management data is not proof of absence.

evidence_requirements: Provide the canonical base/child policy and rule-collection-group/collection hierarchy, priorities and delegated ownership. Preserve both duplicate D07.12 GUIDs as separate recommendations.
Supply representative, time-bounded rule hit/frequency evidence and the ordering rationale; inherited collections and network-before-application processing must be considered.
Reviewer decision: does the organization of groups/collections reflect actual use and ownership without changing required rule behavior? Names, counts and priority values alone cannot answer this.
recommendations.limitations: Frequency-based organization is an operational/design judgment. No log query, synthetic traffic, rule rewrite or automatic priority optimization is performed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Bounded typed IP Group membership alongside rule/policy inventory; no optimization score.
evidence_requirements: Map actual rule source/destination references to canonical IP Group IDs or intended prefixes, with membership, scope and ownership.
Compare repeated address intent and equivalent before/after rule coverage; identify empty or separately managed groups and cases where aggregation would overbroaden access.
Reviewer decision: are useful groups/prefixes reused to reduce rule duplication without changing intended access? Merely creating a group is not sufficient.
recommendations.limitations: No arbitrary rule-count threshold, group-presence pass or automatic prefix aggregation. Empty groups can skip referencing rules. Absent Terraform cidrs may be separately managed and remains unknown.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Bounded direct classic DNAT source-address restriction subcheck; group/effective policy sources remain outside that result.
evidence_requirements: Inventory all incoming DNAT rules across classic collections and assigned/inherited Firewall Policy groups; bind exact rule, parent and source IP Group identities.

Review the prepared direct-source subcheck and expand every referenced IP Group. Reject unrestricted *, any, 0.0.0.0/0 and equivalent full IPv4 range sources; missing arrays/groups cannot imply safe restrictions.
Reviewer decision: are all effective incoming DNAT sources specific and intended, including group membership and inherited policy rules? A true direct-address subcheck is not this decision.
recommendations.limitations: The supplied direct classic address subcheck does not expand IP Groups, resolve policy inheritance or prove complete DNAT population. Empty/unknown arrays, unsupported IPv6, malformed values and exceeded bounds do not produce a safe-source subcheck.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Positive subnet/NAT gateway references; no port-demand or failover inference.
evidence_requirements: Provide time-bounded SNAT utilization, demand/concurrency trends, alert destinations and a capacity rationale appropriate to the actual firewall backend/public IP allocation.
Bind any NAT gateway to the exact firewall subnet and verify workload routing, public IP dependencies, downstream allowlists and expected return paths.

Reviewer decision: do monitoring, capacity choices and existing failover validation demonstrate adequate headroom and seamless recovery? Supply previous validation evidence; do not trigger a new failover or scan.
recommendations.limitations: NAT presence and static port-count arithmetic do not demonstrate adequate demand headroom, working monitoring or seamless failover. No arbitrary exhaustion threshold, live metric/log query or traffic/failover test is run.

batches.acceptance_evidence: Actual source review supports useful bounded preparation, not new whole-recommendation predicates. Implementation, checks and merged acceptance remain separate ledger facts.
batches.supported_modes: Explicit AzureRM 4.50.0 raw Terraform with supplied local snapshots and optional plan; reviewed ARM 2024-05-01 and existing no-restore Bicep; saved normalized evidence and injected scoped management-plane detail reads. No new live tenant run.
positive_negative_uncertainty_tests: Typed supplied rule TLS/category-count, VNet DDoS, private endpoint target/state and configured-zone facts; all nine whole outcomes remain manual without explicit valid human review.
Missing/null/wrong-type/unsupported/symbolic/sensitive/bounded facts remain unknown; automatic/manual connection intent and assigned IP never establish approval.
Empty, single or multiple configured zones never determine backend redundancy or an SLA; preserve current source caveat through reports and review preparation.
Canonical positive subnet/VNet joins; missing/inaccessible/conflicting/wrong-type identity evidence cannot become completeness or a negative relationship.
Exact historical bytes, original control hashes, source bindings, comparison, replay/privacy, prepared review context and no invented decisions.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Supplied application-rule terminateTLS booleans and policy/deployed SKU facts, not an effective TLS-inspection verdict.
evidence_requirements: Map each Premium firewall to its exact effective policy and applicable application rules, including inheritance, bypasses, priorities and HTTPS traffic population.
Provide redacted CA/reference readiness, certificate validity/rotation, managed-identity access and client trust evidence; never submit private keys, certificate material or secret values.

Reviewer decision: do attributable application rules and trust configuration establish TLS inspection for the intended outbound/east-west HTTPS flows, with documented exclusions and observed validation?
recommendations.limitations: Premium capability or terminateTLS=true alone does not establish trusted working inspection. No certificate/secret read, effective-policy expansion, TLS connection or data-plane test is performed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Bounded counts of explicitly supplied application-rule category labels and collection actions; labels themselves are withheld.
evidence_requirements: Provide the approved category policy and exact application-rule collections, actions, priorities, higher-priority exceptions and intended user/traffic population.

Reconcile source versions: current Learn describes categories on Standard and Premium, while pinned AzureRM 4.50.0 documents Premium requirements. Verify the actual supported deployment rather than assigning applicability from one statement.
Reviewer decision: do effective category rules enforce the intended topics, including HTTPS/TLS limitations and privacy-related nontermination categories, without being bypassed by other rules?
recommendations.limitations: A nonzero supplied-label count does not validate category names, feature/SKU support, effective ordering or traffic filtering. No category lookup, URL submission, log query or permission expansion is performed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Bounded firewall/policy/rule and Application Gateway inventory with specific traffic-chain review, not inferred connectivity.
evidence_requirements: Map the actual client-to-gateway-to-Premium-firewall-to-backend path, including routing, Host header, DNS answer and HTTPS port 443 requirements.
Provide redacted evidence that the gateway trusts the firewall CA and that each TLS leg validates the intended certificate/name; never supply certificate or key material.
Reviewer decision: can the intended Application Gateway traffic actually traverse the inspected and re-encrypted chain, including return routing, rather than merely sharing a VNet?
recommendations.limitations: Resource presence, TLS booleans or address/name similarity cannot establish this routed trust chain. No DNS, packet, endpoint, certificate or data-plane probe is run.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Original-time firewall/policy/rule inventory to reconcile against an owner-supplied versioned backup and restore record.
evidence_requirements: Map every effective firewall policy, classic rule set and inherited dependency to a versioned backup artifact or complete source-controlled IaC, including explicit coverage gaps.

Provide redacted artifact references/hashes, backup timestamps, retention/access controls, responsible recovery role and a successful reviewed restore-test record meeting the agreed recovery objective.
Reviewer decision: is the intended firewall rule population recoverable from those artifacts, not just represented by a current assessment report or a backup-resource name?
recommendations.limitations: LandingLens assessment/replay bundles intentionally omit full rules and secrets; they are not firewall backups. Inventory presence does not establish backup completion, retention or recoverability. No backup/restore job or infrastructure action is executed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit configured zone identifiers only; never backend placement, migration status or an SLA verdict.
evidence_requirements: Record cloud, region, deployment context and required resilience; compare against the reviewed current zone-redundant-by-default rollout guidance and applicable service agreement.

Reconcile configured zones with platform migration evidence: the 2026-11-04 guidance says backend placement may not appear in ARM/JSON/ARG. Empty or single configured zones are not proof of backend nonredundancy.

Reviewer decision: does attributable current platform/region evidence establish the required redundancy? For new eligible deployments follow the documented omission/default path; do not add explicit zones solely to satisfy this checklist.
recommendations.limitations: Current Microsoft guidance recommends omitting explicit firewall zones in compatible regions. Configured zone counts cannot safely pass/fail this recommendation or establish an SLA because backend migration may be invisible. No region capability scan or availability test occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Typed explicit VNet DDoS flag/plan reference and unique positive firewall-subnet-VNet links, not complete protected-population coverage.
evidence_requirements: Bind each applicable VNet-hosted firewall and public endpoint to its actual hosting VNet and DDoS protection plan; identify unsupported or unclassified relationships.
Use explicit VNet enableDdosProtection and plan IDs as configuration evidence only. Distinguish Network Protection from per-IP protection and identify the documented Virtual WAN exclusion.

Reviewer decision: is the intended firewall deployment population covered by the appropriate configured protection, with applicability and exceptions supported rather than inferred from one plan's existence?
recommendations.limitations: Positive canonical links do not establish population completeness or mitigation effectiveness. Missing/denied VNet or plan evidence stays unknown; Virtual WAN applicability requires explicit context. No attack, scan, billing read, permission change or additional relationship enumeration occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Exact supplied subnet route-table/NSG references and specific per-service control-plane review.
evidence_requirements: Identify every injected service/subnet, its deployment mode, and the current service-specific allowed routes, NSG ports/service tags and delegation restrictions.

Reconcile exact attached route-table/NSG IDs with effective routes, BGP/peering, rule priorities, service tags and any default-route appliance requirements; missing relationships are not safe negative evidence.

Reviewer decision: do those service-specific paths preserve management/control-plane reachability, including return traffic, without treating any 0.0.0.0/0 route or NSG presence as automatically broken?
recommendations.limitations: Generic route/NSG configuration cannot establish per-service reachability. Standalone Terraform associations require separate evidence and are not inferred. No service inventory expansion, route query, packet, port or control-plane health probe occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Bounded private endpoint subnet/target/explicit connection-state facts, not shared-service applicability or working private access.
evidence_requirements: List shared PaaS services and required subresources, verify actual Private Link availability, and map each applicable target to its exact private endpoint and subnet.

Provide explicit connection approval and correct private DNS/routing plus service public-network controls. An assigned IP or automatic-approval intent is not approval; Approved alone does not prove DNS or public-access restriction.
Reviewer decision: does supported private connectivity cover every intended shared service/subresource and client population, with unavailable services and intentional exceptions documented?
recommendations.limitations: Resource existence or Approved state is not a reachable private-only path. Raw Terraform/plan does not expose approval state; aliases remain unresolved. No approval action, DNS/packet probe, public-access inference or service availability query is performed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Private endpoint target/state inventory plus specific on-premises private-peering and DNS evidence requests.
evidence_requirements: Map each on-premises client network to the intended approved service/subresource private endpoint, including private DNS forwarding/resolution to its private address.
Provide attributable ExpressRoute private-peering, VNet/gateway/route and return-path evidence. Distinguish this from Microsoft peering or VPN access and identify public-internet fallback paths.
Reviewer decision: do representative original-time path records establish the intended private-peering access without public internet transit for the relevant clients and services?
recommendations.limitations: An ExpressRoute circuit or approved endpoint alone cannot establish an end-to-end private path. Terraform connection intent never supplies approval. No peering enumeration, DNS lookup, traffic capture, packet probe or data-plane access is added.
